result.document_summary: Massachusetts General Laws c. 40P § 4, the statewide prohibition on municipal rent control with a narrow exception for cities or towns that accept the chapter.
result.notes: The document gives no effective date, so effective_date is left empty. The statute is a state-level bar on local rent control and is recorded as a rent_increase_limits rule of MA. The exception depends on a city or town accepting chapter 40P, which the document does not say any city has done.

rules.title: State prohibition on municipal rent control (with narrow voluntary-compliance exception)
rules.requirement: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. A municipality that accepts chapter 40P may adopt only a voluntary, compensated program that cannot cover units owned by persons or entities owning fewer than ten rental units or units with a fair market rent over $400.
rules.key_value: Rent control banned; exception only for voluntary, municipally compensated program
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.coverage_text: Applies to every city and town in Massachusetts, barring local rent control of residential rental units.
rules.exemptions_text: A city or town that accepts chapter 40P may adopt voluntary rent control regulation meeting conditions (a)-(c); such regulation may not apply to units owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units or to units with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.interaction: This state law preempts local rent control by Massachusetts municipalities, including Boston and Cambridge, unless a municipality accepts chapter 40P and adopts only the voluntary, compensated regulation it describes.
